entry.title: [NEW] MAL-2026-17893: Malicious code in buyerdashboard (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in buyerdashboard (npm)

Affected:

  • buyerdashboard

buyerdashboard@45.3.4 describes itself as "User dashboard IP info". Its preinstall hook runs `node index.js` on npm install and requests `https://realwbx.com/ip.php?ip=8.8.8.8` with the hardcoded Authorization value `8eb5e8641a5795b022d68e14d8858415`, which differs from the value in each of the account's other packages. The npm account conx3993 published it on 2026-10-15, one of 9 packages from that account between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-15 whose preinstall hook calls realwbx.com.

References:

  • https://www.npmjs.com/package/buyerdashboard

entry.title: [UPDATED] MAL-2026-17870: Malicious code in @mntv-analysis/ui-components (npm)
entry.content:
Malicious code in @mntv-analysis/ui-components (npm)

Affected:

  • @mntv-analysis/ui-components

npm user 'conx3993' published this package in a dependency confusion campaign. It squats a name that looks like an internal package and uses version 50.1.1 so misconfigured resolvers pick it over the real one. Version 0.0.0-stage is an empty placeholder. A 'preinstall' hook runs 'index.js', which poses as an IP geolocation helper. On install it sends an HTTPS GET to attacker-controlled host realwbx.com (/ip.php?ip=8.8.8.8) with a hard-coded 'Authorization' value ('ba95f7810845c0347d6a88d157933c81') unique to this package, then discards the response. The token tells the operator which internal package name the victim installed, and the request reveals the victim's public egress IP. --- _-= Per source details. Do not edit below this line.=-_

entry.content:
Malicious code in kiyoramarkets (npm)

Aliases: GHSA-23wg-cgvp-f8w7

Affected:

  • kiyoramarkets

This package is part of a large family (100+ identified as of September 2026) of near-identical forks of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that inject a covert channel-subscription action into the WhatsApp socket layer. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-76p7-773f-r4q5: Cross-site Scripting (XSS) in serialize-javascript
entry.content:
Cross-site Scripting (XSS) in serialize-javascript

Aliases: CVE-2024-11831

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • serialize-javascript — fixed in 6.0.2

A flaw was found in npm-serialize-javascript. The vulnerability occurs because the serialize-javascript module does not properly sanitize certain inputs, such as regex or other JavaScript object types, allowing an attacker to inject malicious code. This code could be executed when deserialized by a web browser, causing Cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. This issue is critical in environments where serialized data is sent to web clients, potentially compromising the security of the website or web application using this package.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-pq7j-f95f-qfcv: Claude Code: Plugin Hash Pin Bypass Allows Bypass of Hash Pinning
entry.content:
Claude Code: Plugin Hash Pin Bypass Allows Bypass of Hash Pinning

Aliases: CVE-2026-86063

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • @anthropic-ai/claude-code — fixed in 2.1.179

The plugin install flow in Claude Code and Claude Desktop checked out a marketplace's pinned commit SHA using `git checkout` without verifying that the resulting HEAD matched the pinned SHA. An attacker controlling a plugin's upstream repository could create a branch named identically to the pinned 40-character SHA, causing the checkout to silently resolve to the attacker's branch tip instead of the reviewed commit, resulting in attacker-controlled code being installed bypassing the pinned hash. Exploitation required a user to install a malicious plugin, pin to a safe hash, and for the plugin source to be hosted on a git host that permitted SHA-shaped branch names. Users on standard Claude Code auto-update have received this fix already. Users performing manual updates are advised to upda…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-x586-xvc8-g7q6: Qwik: Crashing any Qwik Server via Resource thenable
entry.content:
Qwik: Crashing any Qwik Server via Resource thenable

Aliases: CVE-2026-84994

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • @builder.io/qwik — fixed in 1.20.0
  • @qwik.dev/core — fixed in 2.0.0-beta37

### Summary A Qwik server in the default configuration can be crashed with one unauthenticated HTTP request. During qwik-json body parsing, `ResourceSerializer.$fill$` does `Promise.resolve(resource._resolved)`. If `_resolved` is a plain object whose `.then` is a QRL for an unregistered symbol, the async QRL rejects, the rejection is orphaned, and Node terminates the process via its default unhandled-rejection policy. ### Impact One unauthenticated request crashes the server. Looping keeps every replica dead as long as the attacker sends requests.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-88h9-xgvx-hvf2: @grpc/grpc-js: The exact path match matcher incorrectly only applies a prefix match for case-insensitive matches
entry.content:
@grpc/grpc-js: The exact path match matcher incorrectly only applies a prefix match for case-insensitive matches

Aliases: CVE-2026-101914

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • @grpc/grpc-js-xds — fixed in 1.13.1
  • @grpc/grpc-js-xds — fixed in 1.14.1

### Impact When using RBAC to apply authentication rules, the exact path (method name) matcher applies a prefix match instead of an exact match for case-insensitive matches. As a result, if a service has a method with a name that is a prefix of the name of a different method, and they have different access rules, and case-insensitive matching is used, this bug can cause improper authentication. ### Patches This vulnerability is fixed in 1.13.1 and 1.14.1. ### Workarounds This problem can be avoided by enabling case-sensitive path matching.
